hello: You are probably here because you are hiring, or building something. Here is what I do right now:
lede: I have built and run platforms end to end: payments, search, support, shipping, compliance. In-house, with AI agents, and with the audit trail that makes every change traceable.
note: From consulting to full technical ownership. I know both sides: the process, and the code.

work.title: Work
work.lead: If you only read one entry, read the first. The rest shows how I got there.

cto.text: Overall responsibility for strategy, development, and operations of the marketplace and ERP platform. Next.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Turborepo, Railway, Cloudflare. Commission models and payouts stay configurable, so a new market does not require a code change.

ecommerce.text: Product responsibility for the online shops: roadmap, Shopify, and the connections to warehouse and customer service.

engineer.text: An Angular 19 application in an Nx monorepo, UI from Figma with Tailwind, and interfaces over OpenAPI and RxJS.

projects.title: Projects
projects.lead: Reading about it is one thing. Here are three things you can click: the store I run today, Wire's source, and the thesis code.
projects.note: Wire fetches sources, keeps an index, and asks Jev one yes/no question. The repository is public.

wire.where: Python · Qdrant · Jev · one process, many desks
wire.text: Wire reads a set of sources on a schedule, keeps an index, and asks Jev one yes/no question about every new story. Which sources, how often, which question — that is a desk.

events.text: The backend from my thesis: an event manager with staff, lines, business units, feedback and votes. Written in 2023 entirely by prompting chat-based AI models — the experiment the thesis is about. Archived unchanged.

smartport.text: The marketplace I run as CTO: storefront, seller payouts, search, shipping and compliance on one platform. Not a demo — this is the shop that takes orders.

education.title: Education
education.lead: Two lines. The thesis is the interesting one if you work with AI in the browser.
education.text: Bachelor's examination on 19 December 2023. The thesis at Randstad Digital looks at what chat-based AI models can carry in web development, and where they stop.

offer.meta: AI consulting for small businesses in Rhine-Main | Robin Prause
offer.description: More time for your real work: I come along with small businesses in Frankfurt and Rhine-Main, find the task that eats the most time and set it up for a fixed price.
offer.service: AI and automation for small businesses

hero.lede: I come along while you work, find the task that eats the most time and take it off your hands. You don't have to deal with AI yourself.
hero.hint: Coming along is free in the first year. The price is fixed before the work starts.
hero.by: Robin Prause from Rodgau near Frankfurt. For small businesses, freelancers and private people.

flow.label: Example workflows
flow.note: You decide on anything important: quotes, replies to customers and payments arrive as drafts, and you approve them with one click.

a.d: as a PDF in the shared inbox

b.d: supplier, date, amount and number are read out

c.d: named to a fixed pattern, in the right monthly folder

d.d: for example in Lexoffice or sevDesk

a.d: hedge trimming, 40 metres, by the end of March

c.d: type, place and urgency: call today

d.t: Quote is ready as a draft
d.d: in your template, with your prices

b.d: date, place, work done and hours

c.d: the photos are filed with it

gain.title: What you gain
gain.text: That much time comes back from a single task that costs two hours a week today.

fast.d: Requests are sorted, quotes are prepared.

evening.d: The office stays closed at night and at the weekend.

own.d: Accounts and data belong to you, and your people can run it on their own afterwards.

partner.d: If you like, I stay on after the handover.

top.title: The most used automations
top.lead: These tasks cost a lot of time in almost every business. The easiest place to start is usually the office, with invoices and bookkeeping.

one.d: Supplier, date and amount from an emailed invoice appear in your accounts by themselves.

two.d: Every email lands in the right folder, the right person is told, and a reply is waiting as a draft.

three.d: Customers get a personal confirmation within a minute, and you get a short note.

four.d: The request turns into a draft with your prices. You check it and send it.

five.d: Friendly reminders go out on time, and paid invoices are ticked off by themselves.

six.d: Customers pick a free slot and get a reminder the day before.

seven.d: Every month all receipts are collected and handed over, with no searching.

top.more: That is only the start. The catalogue lists more than 60 further examples, sorted by area: office, customer requests, appointments, marketing, team, purchasing and an overview for the owner.

how.title: How we work together
how.lead: We start small: set up one task properly and see how much time it saves. Then comes the next one.

one.title: Coming along
one.text: I come to you and walk along. I watch what you do and ask questions. One question often helps: what would run short first if twice as many customers came tomorrow? That is where we start.
one.meta: Usually half a day to a full day, free in the first year

two.title: The job
two.text: You get a fixed sum for exactly one task. The sum is set before the work starts. I set the task up with standard tools in your account.
two.meta: Fixed price, set up within a few weeks

three.title: Handover
three.text: We practise until it sticks. After that you can run, change and fix the task yourselves. You get a short guide in your own words.
three.meta: With a guide in your words

four.title: Ongoing support
four.text: You carry on alone, or I stay your contact for a fixed monthly sum. I keep everything running, bring new things along and take on the next task.

five.title: Custom build
five.text: Sometimes a task needs a tool of its own, for example an app for the team. A custom build follows a first job, because by then I know your business well. The code is yours.

check.title: How we recognise a good task
check.one: It comes up at least every week.
check.two: It costs the business about two hours a week in total.
check.three: A person checks the result before it goes out.
check.four: It runs with standard tools in your name.
check.five: It is set up and practised within a few weeks.

price.title: Offers and prices
price.lead: Each offer is a task you can get rid of. I name the exact price after coming along.
price.note: You pay for the tools themselves monthly, directly to the provider. I tell you these costs before we start.

mail.d: Incoming emails are sorted by type and have a draft reply. You check and send.

quotes.d: A request, a note or a voice message turns into a draft in your template, with your prices.

reports.d: Speak briefly into the phone or take a photo. It becomes a clean report or proof of work.

dates.d: Suitable times come from your calendar, and customers get a reminder the day before.

letters.d: Letters from authorities are summarised in plain words, and deadlines are in the calendar.

solo.d: Each of these tasks is also available for one person, usually done in one to two weeks.

ai.title: AI tools that respect data protection
ai.lead: Since February 2025 the EU AI Act requires every company that uses AI tools at work to make sure its people can handle them. That applies to businesses of every size.

desk.d: Company accounts for ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot or Google Gemini in your name, with a data processing agreement.

rules.d: One to two pages in your words: which data may go into the tool and who checks results.

training.d: Training on site with your own tasks. Each person gets a certificate of attendance.

pack.d: Workplace, rules and training together, in two to four weeks.

agent.d: It handles several steps in a row and puts the result in front of you for approval.

connect.d: Data you type in by hand today moves to the right place by itself.

auto.d: Reminders, monthly overviews and payment reminders run on schedule.

fresh.d: It says clearly what you do. The form asks for what matters, and domain and account are in your name.

update.d: Clear text, a good look on the phone and a form that sorts requests.

google.d: Services, opening hours and photos up to date. Replies to reviews are ready as drafts.

build.title: Custom builds: apps and tools for the team
build.lead: A custom build is the second step after a first job. The code is yours, and it runs in your account.

app.d: Made for your workflow, on the phone, the tablet or at the office. For example to record deliveries right at the gate.

own.d: When standard tools reach their limit, for example with industry software that has its own interface.

care.title: Ongoing support: one fixed contact
care.lead: Support starts after the first job and can be adjusted monthly.

basic.d: I keep your tasks running, install updates and answer questions by email and phone.

plus.d: Everything in Basic. Plus one meeting a month, small adjustments and new things that suit you. I take on the next task.

build.d: Add-on for your own software: running it in your account, updates, security and small fixes.

home.title: For private people
home.lead: Work piles up at home too. Here I charge by the hour.

paper.d: Emails, letters and documents sit in clear folders, and deadlines are in the calendar.

smart.d: Lights, heating and devices work together, for example with Home Assistant or Philips Hue.

helper.d: It helps plan the week, summarises emails and reminds you of appointments, in your account.

learn.d: One hour one-to-one, on site or by video. We practise with your own questions.

data.title: Your data stays with you
data.lead: Good automation needs trust. That is why the same principles apply to every job.

avv.d: We sign a data processing agreement before I work with your data. For the tools we use company accounts whose provider offers one.

host.d: The workflows I set up for you run on servers in Germany. Where a tool processes data elsewhere, I tell you beforehand.

name.d: Accounts, data and access belong to you. You keep the overview at all times.

less.t: Only the data that is needed
less.d: We decide together which data goes into the tool and which does not.

human.d: Quotes, replies to customers and payments only go out after your approval.

health.d: Only with a separate, specially protected setup. For practices we start with workflows that involve no patient data at all.

about.title: Who I am
about.one: I have gathered a lot of hands-on experience with platforms, workflows, data protection and programming. Today I am responsible for the technology of a marketplace platform as its CTO.
about.two: With you, though, your business is the focus, not the technology. I listen, look at your daily work and set up exactly the task you want to get rid of.
about.three: I only take on a few businesses at a time, so each one has my full attention. I live in Rodgau near Frankfurt and come to you.
about.who: Small businesses of up to 20 people where the owner decides, for example landscaping, waste disposal, farming and service businesses. Also freelancers, the self-employed and private people.

ai.q: Do we need to know about AI?
ai.a: You know your work, and that is enough. I take care of the technology and practise with you until you can do the task on your own.

cost.a: In the first year, coming along is free. Afterwards I name the task and a fixed sum. You decide in your own time.

start.q: Where is the best place to start?
start.a: Usually the office: invoices, emails and quotes. That is where most of the time goes in almost every business. We set up one task properly, and once it runs, the next one follows.

auto.q: Does everything run fully automatically then?
auto.a: Routine work does. You decide on anything important: quotes, replies to complaints and payments arrive as drafts, and you approve them with one click.

own.q: Who owns the accounts and the data?
own.a: You do. All accounts are in your name, and you pay for the tools directly to the provider. With a custom build, the code is yours as well.

privacy.a: I use company accounts with a data processing agreement and privacy-friendly settings. We decide together which data goes into the tool. A person checks every result before it goes out.

act.q: What is the EU AI Act about?
act.a: Since February 2025 every company that uses AI tools at work has to make sure its people are AI literate. That applies to small businesses too. The training “AI literacy for the team” covers it, with a certificate of attendance.

time.q: How much of our time does this take?
time.a: While I come along, you simply carry on as usual. For practising you plan a few short sessions. After that you save time.

after.a: You can run, change and fix the task yourselves. If you like, you book ongoing support and I stay your contact.

extra.q: Are there costs on top of the prices?
extra.a: You pay for the tools themselves monthly, directly to the provider. I tell you these costs before we start.

end.title: Fancy more free time?
end.text: Tell me in two or three sentences what piles up for you. I reply personally, and we arrange a visit.

privacy.description: What happens to personal data on this site.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What happens to personal data on this site. If the English and German texts ever differ, the German text applies.
privacy.host: The site is hosted by Render Services, Inc., United States, on a server in Frankfurt am Main. Render processes data so the site can be delivered. Because Render is based in the United States, access from there can happen. That rests on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or, where that does not apply, on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
privacy.logs: When a page is opened, the server processes the IP address, date and time, the address requested, the browser identifier, and the status of the response. This is needed to deliver the page and to keep the service secure. It is not used for advertising, and it is not built into a profile. The legal basis is Article 6 (1) (f) GDPR: a working and secure site. The host keeps these logs for its operational period. This site does not keep a log archive of its own.
privacy.storageTitle: Cookies and storage on your device
privacy.storage: This site sets no cookies. There is no analytics and no advertising. Fonts are loaded from this site, not from another provider. If you choose Light or Dark, that choice is stored on your device under the name prause-theme. The reading depth is stored for the browser tab under the name prause-depth and is dropped when the tab closes. The legal basis is section 25 (2) TDDDG: the storage exists for a setting you switch on yourself.
privacy.mail: The form sends your name, email address, and message to mail@robin-prause.de. This site does not store the message. It passes through the Render server in Frankfurt to the Hostinger mailbox, where it stays until I delete it. The basis is Article 6 (1) (b) GDPR when you ask about working together, otherwise Article 6 (1) (f) GDPR so I can answer. The mail link next to the form still opens your own mail program.
privacy.rights: You can ask for access, correction, deletion and restriction, and you can object to processing that rests on legitimate interest. You can also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
privacy.authority: The Hessian Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information, Gustav-Stresemann-Ring 1, 65189 Wiesbaden.
